name: Shibuya
description: Shibuya, Harajuku and Yoyogi Park, out to Sangenjaya's backstreets: the scramble and Hachiko, the city from SHIBUYA SKY, Center Gai's arcades and the streets a famous game drew.

water.note: No sea. The Shibuya River runs in a culvert under the station; its open stretch south of it and the Meguro River from Ikejiri-Ohashi down through Nakameguro are concrete channels drawn at their own level (inland, pipeline/inland_water.py), and so are the parks' ponds.

inland.note: Concrete revetments about 4.5-5 m from the street down to a shallow flow (read from photographs, not measured); the Meguro about 9 m between its walls at Ikejiri-Ohashi and 13 m at Nakameguro, the Shibuya River about 8 m. The ponds at the 5 m laser survey's level.

roofs.note: pipeline/arcades.py (#234): two low PLATEAU-only solids in pedestrian squares (tools/square_huts.py) that the aerial photograph shows are canopies, not huts: a covered walk 3 m wide and 4.1 m tall along the footway by the Yamanote tracks north of the station, and a 2.6 m shelter on an island of the east exit's bus terminal. Each is named by a point inside it, as PLATEAU's footprints have no OSM id.

susuki.note: Susuki (trees.json susuki, #326): on the open grassland and meadows OpenStreetMap maps (natural=grassland, landuse=meadow: the unmown grass of the parks and the hills, where susuki is the grass that stands) (Overture base land, OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL; pipeline/grasses.py). Its heads stand from mid August to spring (web/trees.js).

trees.note: Species are not mapped; the mix is a guess from the cities' street-tree surveys and the parks' own guides: ginkgo and zelkova (keyaki) are Japan's commonest street trees, with plane trees and camphor; the woods are the laurel forest's evergreen broadleaves and camphors, with zelkovas, black pines, maples and a few cedars (sugi, standing for hinoki too). Areas give the parks and precincts known for their own trees a mix of their own; their outlines are OpenStreetMap's (pipeline/tree_areas.py). Somei-yoshino cherries (sakura) line Tokyo's streets after the ginkgo and the zelkova, and stand in the parks' lawns and along the rivers and moats; areas give the places known for them a mix of their own.

areas.name: Hachiko Square's planters
areas.note: The round planter north of Hachiko holds a Somei-yoshino (photographs 2020-25), pruned as a square's trees are: its leaves begin over 3 m up (cherry_plaza, issue 19).

areas.name: Hachiko Square's planters, south
areas.note: And so does the one south of him.

areas.name: Meguro River
areas.note: About 800 cherries on both banks from Ikejiri-Ohashi down through Nakameguro, their branches over the water (Meguro City). In the bloom pink chochin hang along both railings and the cherries are lit after dark (#241): the area is the river's line buffered 14 m, so the railings, about 5.5 m either side of it, are 8.5 m inside the outline.

areas.name: Meiji Jingu
areas.note: The planted shrine forest, now mostly camphor and the evergreen oaks and shii of the laurel forest.

tour.title: Sangenjaya to Harajuku
tour.text: Youth culture's Tokyo: fashion on Takeshita Street, the forest of Meiji Jingu, the busiest crossing on Earth, and out west the izakaya alleys of Sangenjaya where the city goes home to drink.

tour.title: The scramble
tour.text: When the lights change, every crossing turns green at once, the diagonals too, and up to three thousand people cross together. Watch it from above, then join in. Hachiko sits to the south, waiting for his master, as he did for ten years.

tour.title: SHIBUYA SKY, 229 m
tour.text: An open-air deck on Scramble Square's roof, glass at the edge and nothing above you but sky. Come at sunset: Mount Fuji on the horizon, then Tokyo lighting up beneath your feet.

tour.title: Sangenjaya's triangle
tour.text: Between Setagaya-dori and Route 246: a bathhouse, a snack bar, a meat shop open all night. A game drew its hero's home town here and called it Yongen-Jaya; fans still come looking for the café.

protection.title: No sun-access rule for public places
protection.summary: Tokyo protects no park's sunlight. The windows are a lunch-hour thought experiment for this project, as in the Marunouchi model.
protection.source_note: Windows are our own choice (noon to 13:00, all year), not law. The Building Standards Act's shadow rule (日影規制, art. 56-2) limits hours of shadow on neighbouring land in residential-type zones; it does not cover public places and does not apply in commercial districts such as Shibuya.
protection.reading_note: Tokyo keeps standard time all year. Miyashita Park is a roof garden on a mall (2020): its sun here is read at the ground, so treat it with care.
protection.tip: Tip: try a tower on the block south of Yoyogi Park, west of Harajuku Station.

cast.note: the walkers drawn as people, in order (the first ten women and ten men on a desktop, four and four on a phone), each of a body and its clothes no one else in the cast wears (issue 77: the second four of each, built for the crowd) (issue 64: two of the six men were the one argyle sweater vest under two heads, and with the change of clothes unable to touch a black-and-white print, a third of the men at a kerb were that vest): Shibuya's own crowd in everyday clothes, an office worker of each sex, and every fourth a visitor from abroad (the share is an estimate). Passed over (game.js realCast, pipeline/crowd_cast.py): whoever wears a face Kagami wears, and the people the story names

crowd.note: hours: the share of the peak crowd out, by the hour: the morning commute, lunch, and the evening, busiest from 18:00 to 21:00 and busier still on Friday and Saturday nights and at the weekend (Shibuya Redevelopment Association, 2014: 260,000 people a day on weekdays, 390,000 on holidays); few after the last trains (about 00:30)

overture.note: The walk's opening (docs/STORY.md "The walk's opening"; played by game.js startWalk on the story's film engine): the whole of Shibuya from the air at the hour and under the sky the player chose, flown down in one flight to their shoulder at the kerb. Not the story's: no cut, no guide, no words of the case; it comes in from the north-east, high over Omotesando, where the story's opening circles in from the south-west, and it ends behind you at the kerb as the lights change. fly: the camera's one way (points, what it looks at from each, the lens at each), flown at a pace set by its height; the shots are windows on it, for the type and the score. marks: places named as it passes them.

caption.eyebrow: 渋谷スクランブル交差点 · Shibuya Crossing
caption.text: Up to three thousand people cross here at every change of the lights. Tonight there is nowhere you have to be.

walk.note: The walk's people with something to say (web/game/walktalk.js; docs/STORY.md "The walk", "People with something to say"): a few of this evening's locals, each with a small story in parts, each part asking one thing the walk can do. Nothing of the case is in any of them. A part's "then" is what has to happen before the next is said: talk (the next speaker, at once), go (on foot), drive (in your car), up (higher than, as on the roof), photo (a photograph with the point in it, from within r or from above metres over it); meet: someone who, unseen, goes to stand by the next part's speaker.

people.hint: By Hachiko, someone is looking for a friend who is late.
people.title: Which Hachiko

lines: Sorry, have you seen a girl in a green top? Riko. Her hair tied back, always on her phone.
She said Hachiko. My phone died on the Ginza Line.
If you see her across the crossing, tell her I'm by the dog. The bronze one.

then.goal: Find Riko across the crossing, in a green top

lines: Mei? I've been at Hachiko for twenty minutes.
The Hachiko exit. The station's. Oh, no. She means the dog.
Tell her I'm coming round. I'll take the lights.

then.goal: Back across the crossing to Mei, by the dog

lines: There she is.
I did. The dog.

lines.text: Three years in Tokyo, and I still wait at the wrong one.

lines: Thank you. We'd have stood all night on two sides of one name.

after: Everyone says meet at Hachiko. Nobody says which one.
We're going for ramen. She's paying, for the wrong Hachiko.

people.hint: A retired taxi driver with a can of coffee, on the station side of the crossing.
people.title: Once round by car

lines: Thirty years I drove these streets. On foot you only see the bottoms of the signs.
Take your car up to 109 once, where Dogenzaka forks. At night it's another town.
Yours is at a kerb somewhere, isn't it? It'll come to you.

then.goal: Drive to 109, at the foot of Dogenzaka

lines: Well?
109 lit up at the fork, the two roads going up either side of it like a ship's wake.
On the way back, mind the scramble. Green there means the people, not you.

after: The drivers here wait for the scramble like everyone else. Four ways at once, then us.
The rank was quiet till the last trains. Then everyone wanted to go to Setagaya.

people.hint: The vintage shop in Center Gai, at the mouth of the arcade.
people.title: The shot everyone takes

lines: That's a working camera on your chest. Not a phone on a strap.
Everybody shoots the crossing from the café upstairs. The same picture, ten thousand times a day.
Bring me a different one. From right in it, on the green. Or from somewhere higher than the café.

then.goal: Photograph the crossing: from in it, or from high up

lines: Let me see.
Huh. Nobody in it is looking at the camera.
That's the one. Everyone else's has somebody doing a peace sign.

after: Center Gai never sleeps. It does get quieter around five in the morning.
Old cameras come in with the coats. People forget what's in the pockets.

people.hint: The lift at SKY GATE, east of the station.
people.title: Forty-five floors

lines: Going up? The roof is open tonight.
Forty-five floors in the lift, then an escalator out into the air.
Mind your hat at the edge. Come and tell me what you saw.

then.goal: Up to the roof: the lift is behind Yuna

lines: You're back. People always come down quieter than they went up.
What I like is the crossing from up there. All those people, and not a sound.

after: The roof closes in strong wind or lightning. Tonight: {sun_line}
You take people up, and you bring them down. That's the job.

people.hint: A photographer on SHIBUYA SKY's roof, by SKY EDGE.
people.title: Above the crossing

lines: From up here the scramble is a clock face. Everyone waits, then everyone goes.
But from this roof it's always the same angle. I want it from straight above, with the lights on.
That helicopter on the pad. You can fly it? Then take it over the crossing and photograph it from the air.

then.goal: Fly the helicopter over the crossing and photograph it from the air

lines: Let me see.
All four ways at once, from above. The white lines like the spokes of a wheel.
That's the one I could never take. Next time I'm coming with you.

after: {sun_line}
From up here the scramble is a clock face: everyone waits, then everyone goes.

aoi: Stand on one corner for a whole change of the lights, just once. Everyone should.

lines.on_open: Every walk done. Report back to Aoi by QFRONT, across the scramble from Hachiko.

quests.title: Hachiko
talk: ようこそ渋谷へ! I'm Aoi. I guide pilgrims: people who come to stand where a story stood. This month it's ten years since a film and a game put these streets on the map.

You've just crossed it: the scramble, up to three thousand people at one change of the lights. Hachiko, back across the road, has sat there since 1948, and a game called his square Station Square. Cross back to him when the lights change.
Want to see it from above? The lift at SKY GATE in Scramble Square, just across the road, goes up to SHIBUYA SKY, and a helicopter waits on the roof. A hand up at the kerb (Y) stops a taxi.

steps.text: Meet Shun at the mouth of Center Gai

quests.title: Center Gai
talk: Center Gai. A game called it Central Street and gave it a burger bar that doesn't exist. The arch is real: go and read it.
See the glass passage over the crossing, on the station side? Okamoto Taro's thirty-metre mural, Myth of Tomorrow, hangs inside. A game made that passage a hideout.
For the view everyone came for, go up SHIBUYA SKY on top of Scramble Square. Yuna works the door.

steps.text: Read the arch over Center Gai
Find Yuna at SHIBUYA SKY's street door

quests.title: SHIBUYA SKY
talk: SKY GATE: the lifts run from 14F to 45F at 360 metres a minute. From the 46th floor an escalator takes you out into the open air.
The roof is about 2,500 square metres. The glass is lowest at SKY EDGE, over the scramble. No bags past 46F: the wind takes them.
Press E by the lift door. Or open the map: the roof is on your list of places to go.

steps.text: Ride the escalator out onto the roof
Stand at SKY EDGE, over the scramble

quests.title: SKY EDGE
talk: From up here the scramble is a clock face: everyone waits, then everyone goes.
GEO COMPASS, the raised deck in the middle, points at places you can't see: Mt Fuji, Skytree, Suga Shrine, even Paris and Sydney.
After dark, CROSSING LIGHT: eighteen searchlights. {sun_line}

quests.title: Sangenjaya
talk: Sangenjaya, three tea houses. In a game it's Yongen-Jaya, four: the same backstreets with one more tea house.
The game's café has the front of a snack bar here, New Marina. The bathhouse was Chiyo-no-yu, across the lane: closed now, its board still up.

The pilgrims' walk: up from Route 246 past Pukuichi, the café's lane and the bath's board, the stair corner past the Thai place, the fork where the bars' signs stand and the covered passage, then round to Hanamasa and the batting centre's stair. Each stop stamps your passport.
Take it slow. These are people's homes and small shops.

quests.title: Chiyo-no-yu
talk: Forty years a regular, until it closed in 2021. The board's still up. 千代の湯 入口, Chiyo-no-yu, this way.
The coin laundry was down the alley, vending machines by the door. They boarded it up in the end.
Come back after dark anyway. The signs light up the triangle between Setagaya-dori and Route 246.

quests.title: Pilgrim
talk: お帰り! A crossing, a bathhouse, a roof 229 metres up. All of it real, and now you've stood in all of it.

Ten years ago a game drew these streets. Now you've walked them. The stairs of Your Name are in Shinjuku: two stops north on the Yamanote Line, and my friend Nao guides there. Or change the time, go up SHIBUYA SKY at night, or just wander.

hero.perches_note: Where you sit and watch the crossing on the walk (web/game/perch.js): the outer corner of the low granite wall round Hachiko's bed on his left (city.py HK_BED: the bed is behind him as he looks north-east to the station's Hachiko exit, its wall 0.48 m over his setts, its end blocks 0.3 m thick), sat across the corner with the legs over it, facing north to the scramble 40 m off, as people sit on the wall in the photographs of the square. The bed's other end faces east, away from the crossing. at: the hips, over the stone; face: the way the seat looks (a unit vector, x east, y north); cam: where the camera stands, from the hips: back (m behind them), side (m to the seat's right; negative, to its left, so that the bed's lantern 0.9 m behind you stays out of the view; on a tall screen the camera also stands a metre further back and 0.6 m higher, and the aim keeps you nearer the middle), up (m over the feet); look: what the camera frames, the scramble's middle.
hero.rounds_note: What stands round in the level and is a fence to a walker however low: Hachiko Square's two planters (city.py HK_PLANTERS), 0.72 m of granite a walker would step up onto, inside a stainless rail 1.69 m from their middle. [x, y, radius to the rail's outside, m].
hero.note: The Scramble and Hachiko Square within 100 m of the junction: carriageway, paint, kerbs, pavements, street furniture and the fronts a player sees, modelled finely (cities/shibuya/hero.py, blender/build_hero.py, docs/HERO.md)

Frame 5's place, the east exit at the foot of Scramble Square where Miyamasu Bridge stood: the Ginza line station's underside, girders, lights and piers, the bus terminal's ground and the fronts round it, modelled finely (cities/shibuya/hero_miyamasu.py, docs/HERO.md, Miyamasu). Fetched only within 60 m of its edge (frame 4's roof and frame 5) and let go past 85 m, so the Scramble's spawn never holds it. Its bake and street share are the Scramble's: hero.js keeps one of each for all levels.

The Ginza line's Shibuya station (2020) over Meiji-dori: the white cladding of its deck's edge, the glazed band over it and the roof of M-shaped white frames every 2.5 m, 44 spans over 110 m, glass up their feet and white panels over the crowns, the gables in glass (cities/shibuya/hero_ginza.py, docs/HERO.md "The Ginza line's station", issue 57). Its finest parts (the frames' sides and feet, the light mullions, the glazing bars, the joints) are its fine model, never fetched on a phone. The city's box under it is capped at the frames' feet (pipeline/stations.py TOP). Plain materials, no picture: fetched wherever the story walks, since it is seen from frame 5 under it, from up and down Meiji-dori, from Scramble Square's roof and from the air.

SHIBUYA SKY's street lift hall just off the tower's north-east corner, frame 4's way up and the walk's: entered from the west through its glass front's two doors under a canopy, the queue facing east to two scenic cars in their glass shaft outside the tower; the tiles, the sign pillar and the forecourt's planks in front (cities/shibuya/hero_skylobby.py, docs/HERO.md "SKY's street entrance", issue 53). floor: its own level floor is walked on where the ground slopes under it (nav.js lift); posts: its glass and its walls, the shaft and the pillar; belts: the queue's. Its bake and street share are the Scramble's: hero.js keeps one of each for all levels.

offices.note: The storeys behind the skin, drawn by the page after dark (web/interior.js offices; cities/shibuya/hero_scramblesq.py offices() writes it): the tile's storey coordinate (shops at 5.4 m to 71.3 m over 1F, offices at 4.55 m), its spandrel, frit and joints, and what each storey is from 1F = 0.

hero.note: Shibuya Scramble Square's curtain wall over the city's own tower, from the street to the roof's deck: blue-green storey-high panes each at its own slight angle, joints stepping floor by floor, the frit thinning up each pane; after dark its storeys behind the glass, offices, shops, restaurants, the sky lobby and the gallery, each lit by its hours (offices; cities/shibuya/hero_scramblesq.py, docs/HERO.md "Scramble Square's curtain wall"). The tallest thing in every frame: fetched anywhere in the story's streets.

SHIBUYA SKY's roof, SKY STAGE, where frame 4 is played and frame 5 lifts off: the dark porcelain deck, GEO COMPASS's raised heliport with its marking and the compass's bearings, its steps lit under the nosings, the glass on its lit shoe, CLOUD HAMMOCK's nets over lawn, the benches, CROSSING LIGHT's searchlights and the escalators' heads (cities/shibuya/hero_skyroof.py, docs/HERO.md "SKY STAGE"). Fetched only when the camera is near the roof in height as well as in plan (zr): never from the street under it.

story.note: The story (web/game/story.js; docs/STORY.md is the whole of it): Blue Hour. An episode is one case played through in one go: seven frames, each one photograph, on one evening that runs from the blue hour into the night. Sumiko, Akira and what happened on 10 October 1964 are invented; the place, the date, the hours and the city's history are real.
story.title: Blue Hour

card.line: Tonight, as the sun goes down, the crossing stops. Somebody in it turns to look at you.

who.note: Who you play, on a screen of its own (story.css 'the title in three screens'; docs/STORY.md 'The title, as a game opens'): what anyone who met Kagami tonight could know, and nothing of the case (the mother, the sister, the camera of 1964 stay in the story).
who.name: Kagami
who.line: Photographs streets for a living, and takes a small office's jobs: a kerb as it stands, before the works begin. Out on a job, whenever anyone rings.
facts: Shibuya, 10 October, 17:14. A kerb at the Scramble, a minute late
A working camera on a black strap, resting on the chest
who.note_line: 鏡: a mirror. The office uses no other name.

W.wears: A camel double-breasted jacket over a black turtleneck, wide black trousers, flats

M.wears: A camel chore jacket over a black shirt open on a T-shirt, black denim, brown shoes

episodes.title: You came late
episodes.line: A job for the office: one photograph of a kerb at the Scramble, at 17:14. You come a minute late, and the whole crossing stops.

afterimage.name: Sumiko 澄子
afterimage.seek: Someone is still moving. Walk to her.

lines.say: 遅かったね。 You came late.

lines: Sixty years I have stood on this kerb, every tenth of October, at this hour. I was not waiting for you.

He said: the Hachiko crossing, when the sky is the colour of the dome before the show. I came straight from the lift at the store, one glove on, and I was here at fourteen minutes past five. He was not.
After his lecture we were taking the night train to Osaka: the Ginga, at twenty to nine. The Milky Way. He chose it for its name, and a planetarium there wanted him. He had both our tickets.
My family had promised me to a man on my brother's works. We were not going to tell them.
A boy pushed this into my hands, here, and ran. Not a word. It is his.
You are the first who has ever turned to look. Take it. There are seven frames left in it.
I cannot see past this kerb any more, and I cannot see a photograph. But that camera still has the tenth of October in it. Raise it to my corner.

goals.stand: Step back from her corner into the light on the ground. Only from there does the camera see what stood beside her.
goals.raise: You hang his camera round your neck. You are in the light: raise it to her corner, and it sees 1964.
goals.shoot: Turn to her corner. What stood beside her comes up inside the frame lines.
goals.aim: Not yet: it is not inside the frame lines. Turn to the corner where she stood.
goals.ready: A board for tonight's sky under the dome, at seven. The lecturer's name is on it: 水野. Take the picture.

steps.say: The camera sees 1964 only from where it was seen. From anywhere else it sees tonight.
From the light, what stood here that evening comes up in the finder, out of the grain.

steps.do: Turn it into the frame lines
steps.say: While it is outside them, an arrow on their edge points to it. Inside, the lines go amber.
The print comes up as tonight, and 1964 comes up through it. Seven frames: no eighth.

lines: The board. Then it is still there, in the glass. Seven o'clock, under the dome: his lecture. He counted stars for a living.
A man does not post his name for seven and fail to come at five. Something stopped him. Find out what, before the frames run out.

relic.name: the planetarium's board
relic.cap: Her corner. The board for his lecture that evening, under the dome.

after: The lights change. Nobody else saw the crossing stop.
In your hand, an old rangefinder. Its counter reads 6. Scratched small into the base plate: 水野. The name on the board.
frames.note: She waited here at 17:14, one glove on. He was to lecture at seven. He did not come.

meet.goal: A name on a camera. The vintage shop in Center Gai will know what it is.
lines: Where did you get this? Nobody has made one like it in fifty years.
水野. Mizuno. Scratched small on the base plate, where his hand would cover it. A careful man. And it loads from below, this one: the whole plate comes off.
And there is a roll in it. Thirty frames gone, six to go. Whatever he took is still in there, asleep. Film waits.
My grandfather had this shop in '64. He used to say people leave themselves behind, where they meant to do a thing and did not. Most are gone by morning. The ones that can never do it stay.
And that a roll like this wakes up one frame at a time, if you stand where the man stood. I thought he was drunk. Come back and tell me.
One more thing. Every year on this night an old man stands on one of the stone cherry blossoms in the square by Hachiko, and looks at the crossing.
Ask him why, and he says somebody stood there once. Stand where the man stood, my grandfather would have said.

frames.goal: Six frames. Go back out under the arch.

goals.shoot: Raise the camera to the boy's pitch at the kerb, towards the crossing.
goals.aim: Turn towards the crossing: his pitch was at the kerb, in front of you.
goals.ready: A shoeshine boy's box and stool at the kerb, and nobody on the stool. Take it.
goals.stand: Stand on the stone cherry blossom in the light: where the man stood.
goals.find: The street has stopped, and nobody in it moves. No light marks where this one was taken from: the old man's stone cherry blossom, in the square by Hachiko. Find it, and raise the camera there.

relic.name: the boy's pitch
relic.cap: The station kerb: a shoeshine boy's box and stool, a hundred yen under his tin, and nobody on the stool.

hints: Four stone cherry blossoms lie round the two planters by Hachiko. Tonight the old man is standing on his, looking at the crossing: stand on it beside him, and the two halves of the line meet.
Hachi knows which. He goes to it and sits there.
A light, on the blossom where the man stood.

after: A shoeshine boy's box and stool at the kerb, a hundred-yen note under his tin, and nobody on the stool. He left his pitch in a hurry, and his money with it.
Five frames. A boy ran from his pitch with a police box thirty steps away.
frames.note: The station kerb in 1964: a shoeshine boy's pitch, a hundred yen under his tin, and the stool empty.
frames.lost: the boy's pitch at the station kerb

frames.goal: A boy ran from his pitch, thirty steps from the police box by Hachiko. Somebody there was on duty. Ask.

afterimage.name: A detective
afterimage.seek: Somebody by the police box is still on duty.
lines: That is the Mizuno camera. I logged it this afternoon, and I lent it back to him for one minute. So. Who are you to him?

ask.q: He is a policeman, and he is waiting.
options: Nobody. I was hired to stand on a kerb with it, and I came late.
His lawyer. I am here for his effects.
Headquarters. I am taking the case over.
right: Late. Then you are the first to tell me the truth in this box today.

lines: In twenty years nobody has lied to me that badly. This box is closed to you.
fail.title: Seen through
fail.line: A detective of 1964 knows a lie when it stands in front of him. The Stop lets go, and the lamp is only a lamp again.

then: Mizuno Akira, twenty-six. Lecturer at the planetarium. He walked in at four o'clock in his lecture suit and said he had pushed a man off its roof.
Kanbara, section chief on the river works. Fell from beside the dome at about ten past three, while the whole city was indoors watching the ceremony.

There was a white glove in the dead man's fist. A lift girl's, from the store over the station. Mizuno says it is his: he picked it up in the store's lift this morning, and Kanbara tore it out of his pocket.
I sent a constable to the store all the same. Every girl at her post all afternoon, says the floor manager. On the day of the Games, a store does not lend its name to a fall.
In twenty years nobody has confessed to me that politely. He asked for one thing: a minute at the kerb, with his camera.

I walked him there myself, a constable on his other side. He took one photograph across the road, gave the camera to a shoeshine boy with a coin, and did not cross. It was his to give. The case was closed.
I watched the boy go into the crowd on the far side, and lost him. I have wondered since what that man bought with his minute.

goals.shoot: Raise the camera to Hachiko. The box where he gave himself up stood beside him.
goals.aim: Turn to Hachiko: a red lamp stands by him.
goals.ready: The police box's lamp, lit, and Hachiko under it. Take it.

lines: That lamp was lit when he came in. He stood under it and gave his name before I had asked.
You do not confess that fast to something you did. You confess that fast to keep someone else out of the room.

relic.name: the police box's lamp
relic.cap: Hachiko, and the red lamp of the police box where he gave himself up.

ask.q: A lift girl's glove in the dead man's fist. She told you herself: she came from the lift with one glove on. He is waiting for you to say it.

options.text: It was her. Hayase Sumiko was on that roof.
say: Then you have said what he would not. I closed it on his word within the hour. Be surer than I was.

file.say: You said it at the police box: it was her. Hayase Sumiko was on that roof.

options.text: Not yet. A glove says who he held, not who pushed him.
say: Good. I had a glove and a confession, and I stopped looking. Do not.
options.file: You would not name her on a glove alone.

then: It was not my case to reopen. It is not mine now.

after.say: You have said it aloud: the girl at the kerb, who put the camera in your hand.
A lift girl's glove in the dead man's fist. She told you herself: she came from the lift with one glove on.

after: He came. He stood across the street between two policemen, and did not cross.
Four frames. The planetarium's roof is gone. The only place it can still be seen from is above.
frames.note: He came, under arrest, and did not cross. He had confessed within the hour. In the dead man's fist: a lift girl's white glove.
frames.lost: the lamp he gave himself up under

meet.goal: Go up. The lift at Shibuya Scramble Square, east of the station.
lines: The roof? Forty-five floors in under a minute.
My grandmother ran a lift in the old store over the station. White gloves, a little hat. She said the job never changes: you take people up, and you do not ask them why.
She said the Hayase girl went over to the planetarium on her break, the day of the ceremony, and came back with one glove. Nobody asked her why, either.
The police came round the store that evening, asking whether all the girls had been at their posts. The floor manager said yes. My grandmother said nothing, and was sorry for it all her life.

frames.goal: Take the lift, then the escalator to the roof.

afterimage.name: Kanbara
afterimage.seek: Up here the city has stopped too. One man is at the east glass, looking down at where his roof was.
lines: You are not him either. I went up there for a roll of film. The lecturer photographs the sky from that roof every clear night, and my works are at the bottom of every picture. The stars in a picture tell the night it was taken, to the hour.
There is a night in September I want nobody to have a picture of.

The girl came up instead. My intended, her family says; she will not look at me. I took her wrist and asked where he keeps his film. She tore loose, left me her glove, and ran. I was still on my feet. Write that down.
Then somebody came up the iron stair behind me, while they drew the rings in the sky. I was watching the rings. I never turned round.

goals.stand: Stand at the glass beside him, in the light: the edge of the roof on Hikarie's side.
goals.shoot: Hold the camera out over the glass, where he is looking: straight down, at the foot of the towers. The camera remembers what stood there.
goals.aim: Lower. Straight down over the glass, at the foot of the towers.
goals.ready: The dome, inside the tower that replaced it. Take it.
goals.find: No light marks it this time. Stand at the glass beside him, and look where he looks: down, at where the dome stood.

lines: Is it there? The dome? …Then look at the street at its foot. That was my river. At three I looked down into the cut from the parapet: not a soul in it. I had sent them all home to the ceremony.
The stair was iron, and what came up it was nailed boots. Every man on my works wore them. So did the lecturer, at night, when he went up with his camera.

lines.say: You have the girl's name in your mouth. Spit it out: I was on my feet when she ran. Those were not a girl's shoes.
Sixty years I have asked: whose glove. I should have asked: whose boots.

relic.name: the dome
relic.cap: From the roof: the planetarium's dome, inside the tower that stands there now, and the street at its foot where his works were.

ask.q: Nailed boots on the iron stair, after she ran. Two men you have heard of tonight wore them.

options.text: Mizuno. He confessed to it within the hour.
say: The lecturer? Then he let the girl run, and came back up after her. Ask yourself what for.

file.say: You named the boots on the stair: Mizuno's.

options.text: A man from the works below.
say: One of mine. …Then I signed for the boots myself.

file.say: You named the boots on the stair: a man from the works.

say: Nor could I. I never turned round.

hints: A pace from him along the glass, on Hikarie's side: the edge of the roof he is looking over.
Hachi knows the place. He goes to it and sits there.
A light, at the glass beside him.

after.say: At Hachiko you said it was her. The roof says otherwise, and you take it back.

after: She tore free of a living man and ran. Then nailed boots came up the stair while he watched the rings. At three the cut below was empty: he had sent his men home.
Three frames. Kanbara's works: the river that was put under the street, at the foot of the tower across the road.
frames.note: From the roof the whole cut can be seen, and at three it was empty. She left him alive. Then nailed boots came up the stair: his works wore them, and so did the lecturer.
frames.lost: what came up the stair after her

file.say: On the roof you took it back: those were not a girl's shoes.

frames.goal: The river runs under the street here, at the foot of the tower.

afterimage.name: Hayase Tatsuo
afterimage.seek: A man in work clothes is standing where the river went under.
lines: You have been up on the roof. I can see it on you.
Hayase. Foreman on the river. We put it under the street in time for the Games, and nobody will thank us for it.
The tenth? I was down in the cut all afternoon. The gang was off for the ceremony, and somebody had to mind the pumps. Nobody from my gang went up on any roof.

ask.q: He has told you where he was that afternoon. Which of it will your roll not let stand?

press.say: We put it under the street in time for the Games.
press.no: It is under the street. You walked over it to get here.

press.say: The gang was off for the ceremony.
press.no: Every man of them. The section chief sent them home himself.

press.say: I was down in the cut all afternoon, minding the pumps.
Nobody from my gang went up on any roof.
press.no: Not one of my gang. I know where every one of them was.

ask.show: Then tell him what the roll has against it.
ask.wrong_print: That? That is nothing to me. I was at the pumps till dark.
right: …From the parapet you can see the whole cut. He looked down, did he. And there was nobody at the pumps.
No. I was not in the cut.

lines: You are fishing. A camera full of pictures, and you do not know what is in one of them.
fail.title: He saw through you
fail.line: Half his life on the works: he knows a man who is guessing. The Stop lets go. The roll is in your hand; look at it before you go back to him.

then.say: You had the lecturer for it? All Tokyo will, by morning. It suits me.
A boy of mine drowned in the culvert in September. Kudo Masao, nineteen, up from Aomori for the work. We were pouring at night to be done for the Games, and the river came down on him.
Kanbara wrote him down as a drunk who fell in the river on his night off, and paid me to say the same. I said it. That is the first time I have said his name since.
Last night Kanbara sat at our table, my sister's intended, and told me: if September ever comes out, the book will say the foreman ran the pour.
Today I went up after him, to talk. He was at the parapet with his back to me, watching the rings, a lift girl's white glove in his fist. My sister runs a lift at that store.
I came down the stair alone. On the iron I passed the lecturer going up, two at a time. He never looked at me.
You have nothing that puts a man of mine on that roof. Then I have nothing to say to you.

goals.shoot: He is looking at where his river ran. Raise the camera to the street at his feet.
goals.aim: Look down the street the way he is looking: it was water.
goals.ready: The river, open, and the works' board over it: section chief, Kanbara. Foreman, Hayase. Take it.
goals.stand: Step into the light: from there the street opens the way the water ran.
goals.find: No light marks it this time. He is looking at where his river ran: a few steps from him on Hikarie's side, the street runs straight away from you the way the water ran. Stand there.

lines.say: Open. As it was. …I was on my way to the police box just now, to tell them. At the station they were saying the lecturer had given himself up for it.
So I turned round, and came back here. I will never ask him why he did it.
Open. As it was. …That is all you will have from me.

relic.name: the river
relic.cap: The river, open to the sky, Miyamasu Bridge over it, and the works' board: Kanbara, Hayase.

hints: Six or seven steps from him, on Hikarie's side: from there the street opens straight ahead of you, the way the water ran.
Hachi knows the place. He goes to it and sits there.
A light, where the street opens the way the water ran.

after.say: The lecturer came up the stair after her brother, and was in the police box within the hour. What did he find at the top?
He has told you nothing. The frame that would have opened his mouth was spent on the roof.

after: Two frames. On his stone blossom by Hachiko, an old man has been watching the camera in your hand all evening.

flight.note: Frame 5's way down: the helicopter on the roof's pad, which starts up as the roof's picture is taken and is got into (board); then one flight (path: [x, y, z, t], the film's own path, which every shot covers and none moves) in one wide turn to the right: off the roof to the west-north-west, over the crossing heading north, round the station at 72 m radius and 19 m/s (a bank of 25 degrees), and down from the north onto the open ground north-east of the station, by the river's street, its door towards your spot. Cut as an aerial unit shoots it (docs/STORY.md, The flight): seven shots, every camera on the inside of the turn, the helicopter's right, so it crosses the frame left to right in every one; a camera ship that follows the way it has been going, never whipped round; a cut where it leaves a frame or enters one. A film whose guide is the helicopter (web/game/game.js story ctx board and film; its way checked by tools/flight_clear.py, its steadiness and where it sets you down by tools/heli_flight.js).

board.goal: Get in the helicopter on the pad.

call.note: Why the helicopter: the office rings (the prologue's voice) as the roof's picture has been talked over. The light is going and the kerb was the job; at sunset the queue for SHIBUYA SKY's lifts down is long; the office has its own helicopter on the pad for tonight's pictures from the air.
lines: Kagami. Where are you now? …On the roof of the Scramble tower? The kerb was the job, and the light is going.
The queue for the lifts down is half an hour at sunset. Our helicopter is up there on the pad, for tonight's pictures from the air.
I have told the pilot to set you down by the station first. Go.

caption.text: There is a faster way down than the lift.

shots.note: Locked off low on the roof behind it, as it lifts, hangs, dips its nose and goes off over the edge away from us; the lens pans with it once it moves.
Air to air: the camera ship off its right rear quarter, swinging out to its side as it gathers speed and goes down towards the crossing, a 50 mm lens.

caption.text: From up here the crossing is one thing, breathing in and out.

shots.note: The reveal: high over the crossing to the east, looking down at it, as it passes over heading north and banks into its turn, left to right across the frame.

Inside its turn, low over the crossing: it goes round the station banked towards us, the lit tracks and the towers wheeling behind it; a pan of 66 degrees in nine seconds, the lens drawn in as it goes away.
From a roof to the west, on its right: it comes down out of the lit towers to the north towards its spot, the lens panning down with it; its searchlight on the ground ahead of it.

caption.text: And under the street east of the station, a river nobody has seen since 1964.

shots.note: Locked off on the ground as it comes down into the frame, turns its door to your spot and settles.

frames.note: The river, open, under the works' board: Kanbara, section chief. Hayase, foreman: her brother.
frames.lost: the river his works put under the street

file.say: The foreman passed the lecturer on the stair, coming down. The boots were not Mizuno's.

lines: It's me. I rang the office again. They said you were out on a job. You are always out on a job on the tenth.
I'm at Mum's. Three years today. I lit the incense for both of us.
At the funeral I said don't bother coming any more. I didn't mean for the rest of our lives.
That's all. Ring me, or don't. I'm here.

meet.goal: The old man on the stone blossom by Hachiko. He knows that camera.
lines: That camera. I carried it across this road when I was fourteen. A hundred yen.
You have been using it tonight. Then you have seen where I worked.

ask.wrong: No. I had a box, and a stool, and the kerb in front of me.
right: There. The box my father made, and the hundred yen under the tin. …So it does wake up.

lines: You are showing me any picture at all. I sat there sixty years ago; I know it when I see it.
fail.title: He turned back to the station
fail.line: An old man asked to be shown where he sat as a boy, and was shown somewhere else twice. He will not tell the rest to someone guessing. The roll has his pitch in it: find it before you go back to him.

then: He stood on this stone, between a detective and a constable, and called me over from my pitch. A hundred yen, and one sentence for the girl at the pillar box: tell her to open it.

Halfway across, a policeman on her side turned and looked at me. A shoeshine boy running with a camera like that: I knew what he would think. I pushed it into her hands and ran. I never said it. I never even saw her face.
He did twelve years. He came out in '76 under his mother's name, Hoshino, and came looking for the boy. He asked me whether she had heard it. I said yes.

Sixty years I have had it in my mouth. He took a room in Sangenjaya, fifteen minutes down the old tram line, and printed photographs for an office for thirty years. Forty years we shared a bath-house, and I never took it back.

Every tenth of October at sunset he stood at my old pitch, on the kerb, for one minute, and looked at her corner: the corner, not the people on it. Then he went home. I stood here behind him every year. He never once turned round.
Last year he said he would cross at last. The lights went green, and he stepped back. He went in March.

I witnessed his will. It paid for one thing: a photograph of her corner at fourteen minutes past five today, before they take up the kerb on Monday. The word on your plan is in his hand. You were a minute late.
The last one he took is still in there. Stand where he stood.

frames.goal: Stand where he stood: at the boy's pitch, in your second print.
frames.goal2: The station kerb, straight across the crossing from her corner: where the boy's box stands in your second print.

afterimage.name: Mizuno Akira
afterimage.seek: On the station kerb, an old man in the stopped crowd is looking across the road.
lines: Is she there? I can never see past the road.
That afternoon I was in the darkroom under the dome, printing the slides for my lecture. When the jets came over for the rings, I ran up to the roof to take them.
He was below the parapet with her glove in his fist. I knew it: a darn in the thumb, in blue thread. I had watched her sew it on the tram.
I walked to the police box by her corner and said I had pushed him.
They gave me one minute at this kerb, a policeman on each side. Had I crossed to her with those two beside me, they would have asked her why.
So I took her picture from here, and sent the boy across with the camera and one sentence. Years after, he told me she had heard it. She never came. I supposed she had opened it, and decided.
You have my camera. Then take it again. The one I took.

goals.stand: Stand where he stood, at the kerb's edge.
goals.shoot: Face her corner, as he faced it.
goals.aim: Turn to her corner, across the crossing: something red stands there.
goals.ready: Her corner as he saw it: the pillar box, her umbrella, the board for his lecture. Take it.

lines: The board is in it? Seven o'clock. …I never gave that lecture.
What I could not carry across, I put under the base plate, in the dark, with one word in pencil. Do not look yet. There is a frame left in there, and light kills what is inside.
I wrote: wait. When I came out it was twelve years on, and she had a life. I did not mean for the rest of hers.
Carry it over to her. I never could.

relic.name: her corner
relic.cap: From his kerb: the pillar box she waited by, her umbrella at its foot.

after: He left something under the base plate. She has held that camera for sixty years and never opened it.
One frame. Carry it across to her.

ride.name: Hachiko
ride.line: Two frames. Your car is coming round to take you back to Hachiko.
ride.board: Your car is at the kerb. Get in.
ride.riding: Back to Hachiko, the long way round the station.

frames.note: His own frame, taken again. Whatever he meant her to have is under the base plate.

stirs.line: Across the road, in the held crowd, an old woman has turned towards you.

frames.lost: her corner as he saw it
hints: The station kerb, straight across the crossing from her corner: where the boy's box stands in your second print.
Hachi knows the kerb. He takes you there.

meet.goal: Carry his camera across the road to her kerb.
lines: 遅かったね。 You came late.
That was me, the first time, too. You thought it was the girl. She is only what I left here.
Hayase Sumiko. Eighty-four. I have stood at this kerb every tenth of October since I was her.
That camera. …It is in my bag. It has been in my bag every tenth of October for sixty-two years. And it is round your neck.
You have been all over Shibuya with it tonight. Before you tell me anything, let me see what you know.

ask.q: Who was behind Kanbara at the parapet?
ask.show: Show me which of your prints puts him there.
ask.lost_q: You have no picture of the river to show me. Then without one: who was behind Kanbara at the parapet?
ask.wrong_print: Perhaps. But not because of that picture. Show me the one that puts him there.

wrong_by.sumiko: I tore free and ran, and left him on his feet with my glove in his fist. The man on the roof told you so himself.
wrong_by.akira: He ran up the stair for the rings and found him already down. Somebody came down that stair as he went up.
wrong_by.kanbara: He did not go over by himself. He never turned round to see who it was; you need not do the same.

wrong.say: Think of the roof. The man there told you what came up the stair behind him. Not a girl's shoes.
The roof would have told you, and you spent it. Think who else stood to lose by what happened in the river.

ask.right: Tatsuo. Yes. He told me himself in 1989, the week he died. By then there was no Mizuno anywhere to find.

lines: You carried his camera all over Shibuya tonight and did not look at what it gave you. Go and look. I have waited sixty years; I can wait while you do.
fail.title: She is not answered
fail.line: Two answers wrong. She turns back to the road. Take it up again from her kerb: the roll is in your hand.

ask.q: Why did Akira not cross the street? Tell me whom he was keeping out of it.
ask.show: Show me which of your prints says so.
ask.lost_q: You spent the police box, so you never heard what was in the dead man’s fist. Then tell me without it: whom was Akira keeping out of it?
ask.wrong_print: That is true. But that picture does not say it. The one that does has the glove in it.

wrong_by.tatsuo: He passed my brother on the stair and never looked at him. He did not know whose boots they were. Think what was in the dead man's fist.
wrong_by.akira: Himself? He walked into the police box of his own accord. Think what was in the dead man's fist.
wrong_by.tanaka: Nobody was going to ask a shoeshine boy anything. Think what was in the dead man's fist.

ask.wrong: The detective gave him his minute. He could have crossed. Think what the glove told him.
right: Me. …He knew my glove. He thought I had done it.
And I believed he had done it, for me. Kanbara was the man my family meant me to marry.
If I had said I was on that roof, it would have been murder for a woman. Without me it was a quarrel over a roll of film. So I said nothing, and I never went to him. They would have asked me why.
Twelve years I ran my lift, and came here on the tenth. You take people up, and you do not ask them why.

ask.q: A boy pushed his camera into my hands, here, and ran. Who was he?
ask.show: Show me which of your prints says it.
ask.lost_q: You spent the boy’s pitch. Then from what you were told tonight: who was the boy?
ask.wrong_print: Yes. But that picture does not say it. Show me where he sat.

wrong_by.akira: He stayed on his kerb, between two policemen. He sent someone.
wrong_by.detective: The detective lost the boy in the crowd. He told you so himself.
wrong_by.kudo: That boy was in the river a month before.

ask.wrong: Somebody in the square tonight told you where he sat when he was a boy.
right: Tanaka. The shoeshine boy, grown old. Sixty-two years, and I never knew his name.

ask.q: He ran, and never said a word. Was there nothing to say?

options.text: There was one sentence, and he never said it: tell her to open it.
say: Tell her to open it. He told me once never to open a camera: light kills what is inside. So I never did.
I never had it developed, either. As long as it was shut, there was one picture of his I had not seen.
options.file: You gave her the sentence the boy never said: tell her to open it.

then: Every year I looked east, the way he would come from the dome. Not once across the road.
Take your last one. I have waited sixty-two years; I can wait one frame more.

frames.goal: One frame. Find the place where both kerbs are in it.

meet.say: Every light at the crossing turns green

goals.shoot: Both of them, in one frame. From the middle you can only face one: find the corner that sees both kerbs.
goals.aim: Not yet: one of them is out of the frame.
goals.wait: Hold them both in the frame, and wait.

hints: Not the middle, and not either of their kerbs: from one of the two other corners of the crossing, both of them are in front of you at once.
Hachi knows a corner that sees both. He goes to it and sits there.
A light, at a corner that sees both kerbs.

after: In 1964 you could not cross this junction corner to corner. You can now.
An old woman is crossing, slowly, through everyone, to the kerb where he stood.
frames.note: In the middle of the crossing, every light green: they met.

end.title: Blue Hour

found.line: Your hand is empty: his camera went with the girl. At his kerb the old woman takes the same camera out of her bag, sixty-two years older. You wind the film back into its tin for her, turning the knob until it goes slack, and she takes the base plate off at last. Inside, folded once: her ticket for the night train, 10 October 1964. On its back, in his pencil, one word.

lines: 東京都区内から
大阪市内ゆき
ticket.alt: A card railway ticket of 1964, and its back, with one pencilled word: wait.

line: He took twenty-nine pictures on that roll and is in none of them. In your last frame he is there, and so is she: the first photograph they were ever in together.

line.say: At Hachiko you said her name to a policeman, and on a roof you took it back. He never had the roof.

On Monday the roll goes to be developed, to see what sixty-two years have left on it. Somewhere on it is a night in September with the works' lamps lit under the stars, and Kudo Masao, nineteen, at work.

line: On your phone there is one number you have not rung in three years. You are standing at a kerb. You ring it.
end.next: The counter, at 0, turns over to S. Somebody has loaded a new roll.

overture.note: The episode's cold open, half a minute under a clear sky at blue hour (the story keeps its rain for the last frame): the district from the air with every window and screen lit, down to the street from the height of the kerb, the crossing from above as the title falls, then the kerb behind you as the lights change. No guide, no painted filter: the street as it is.

caption.text: As many as three thousand people cross here at every change of the lights. Every tenth of October since 1964, one woman has waited at this corner.
Every evening, for a few minutes after the sun goes down, this crossing holds its breath.
Nobody has ever noticed. Tonight, you will.

order.to: Kagami: the Hachiko crossing, north-west kerb.
lines: One photograph of the kerb as it stands, before the works on Monday.
Take it at blue hour: the few minutes after sunset when the sky and the street lamps are equally bright, and nothing casts a shadow.
Sunset is at 17:14. The client asked for 17:14, to the minute. Do not be late.
For the estate of A. Hoshino.

plan.note: Pencilled on the old plan of 1964, at that corner. Not ours.

lines: Kagami? You dropped off the line. Where are you? …The Hachiko crossing, the north-west kerb. Good. Late, but there.
A photograph of that kerb, before the works start on Monday. It has not been touched since they laid it in 1964, the week before the Olympics.
The client is an estate: a Mr Hoshino, who printed for us before my time. He asked for it at fourteen minutes past five today, to the minute.
One odd thing. The old plan has a word pencilled on that corner: 待つ. Wait. Nobody here knows who wrote it, or for whom.
And your sister rang again. Today, of all days. I told her what you always have me tell her: that you are out on a job.

guide.line: A dog is walking through the stopped crowd. He looks back at you.

lines: A dog is walking through the stopped crowd. He is coming to you.
He looks up at you, as if you were the one he had been waiting for.

pairs.line: Her corner, and the kerb straight across from it. Forty-odd steps of road. Whatever kept him from her that evening, it was not the distance.
From the police box to the boy's pitch is thirty steps. The one minute he asked the detective for was spent there.
A glove in a dead man's fist says who he held. It does not say who came up the stair afterwards. The case was closed on the glove.
The roof looks straight down into the cut. Anyone minding its pumps at three would have been seen from the parapet, and nobody was.
The same corner, from both kerbs. For fifty years each of them stood at one end of this picture on the tenth of October, and neither looked at the other's end.

overture.note: The overture (docs/OVERTURE.md, web/game/overture.js): Crossing. A petal (a ginkgo leaf in autumn, a snowflake in winter, a mote of light in summer) leaves the edge of SHIBUYA SKY, falls 229 m to the scramble, passes Hachiko, and the screens, and ends on the scramble from across it, into the sun, before the game begins at the kerb (game.start). Crowds are kept at a distance: no shot comes close to them. Points name the landmarks in scene.json, so a rebuilt map moves them.

caption.text: The wind on the roof of Scramble Square, above the busiest crossing in the world.
He met his master's train here every evening, and went on waiting for nine years after he was gone.

caption.text: When the lights change, up to three thousand people cross at once. Tonight, one of them is you.

night.note: After dark: the night after rain, under a falling star. From the stars down to SHIBUYA SKY and its searchlights, over the edge of the roof and down to the scramble, to Hachiko under the lamps, the screens in the wet street, the hush before the lights change, and the crossing itself. The crowd is seen from above and from across the junction; no shot stands among it. wet: the streets wet from a shower that has passed, under a clear sky. show: CROSSING LIGHT on whatever the hour. One meteor crosses the sky, and only where the sky is empty (from the roof, and over the title), never with the searchlights' beams in shot: a comet standing among the searchlights' beams read as a moon throwing light (the owner, November 2026).
